sections.html:
Find the Recorder of Deeds in Suite 209 of the Newton County courthouse, 101 S Wood St, Neosho, MO 64850, on the main floor in the northeast corner. The phone number is (417) 451-8224. The counter opens at 8 in the morning and closes at 4:30 in the afternoon on weekdays, with holidays off.

Watch the clock on closing day. New recordings are accepted only until 3:30 pm, and anything handed in later goes onto the books the next business day in the order received. Marriage licenses stop at 3:00 pm. To send papers by mail, use P.O. Box 604, and email goes to recorder@ncrecorder.org.

sections.h2: What the recorder keeps on file
sections.html:
This office holds the permanent record of who owns land in Newton County. It records warranty deeds, deeds of trust, releases, plats, surveys and powers of attorney, and it keeps military discharges along with state and federal tax liens.

A few limits to know before you call:

  • Staff cannot practice law, so they will not draft a deed, supply legal forms or explain what a filed paper means.
  • The office does not produce abstracts of title or opinions on the status of a title (RSMo 59.200.1).
  • A closing office or lawyer prepares the paper. The recorder indexes it, scans it and keeps the permanent copy.

The land is here, so the deed is filed here. RSMo 442.380 sends any written conveyance of real estate to the recorder of the county where the property sits.

The county fee page shows $26 for page one of a standard document and $3 for every page after it. A flat $2.00 statewide increase under Senate Bill 938 now applies, so call (417) 451-8224 to confirm the figure that will appear on your invoice.

Newton County recording charges

The office keeps an overpayment of up to $10, so a check that runs slightly long will not cause a rejection, provided the payment is never below the statutory fee. A release or assignment covering several items adds $5 for each item after the first.

sections.h2: What a deed must look like before it is accepted
sections.html:
The recorder may reject a paper that fails the layout test in RSMo 59.310, or record it and add a $25 penalty. The office's format page spells out what passes.

  • Paper: 8.5 by 11, white or pale, 20 pound stock, no logos, printed on one side.
  • Text: dark ink at 8 point or larger, with each signer's name typed beneath the signature.
  • Page one: a clear 3 inch band across the top for the recorder's certificate, then the title, date, grantors and their marital status, grantees, the mailing addresses the statute calls for, and the legal description.
  • Margins: three quarters of an inch at the sides and bottom.

Indexing relies on labels. The words grantor and grantee must sit beside the parties, and a house's street address cannot replace a legal description. Some papers are exempt: those signed before 2002, military separation papers, certified copies, documents executed abroad and anything where an original party has died or lacks capacity. A rejected document comes back with the reason stated.

sections.h2: Can Newton County documents be recorded electronically?
sections.html:
Yes. The county has an agreement with iCounty Technologies, LLC, and the contact line for setting it up is (816) 295-1540. The recorder's eRecord page lists same-day recording, payment by ACH and quick correction of a rejected document as the reasons to use it.

If an electronic filing is rejected, you can fix it and resubmit without a courier trip to Neosho. Electronic recording rests on RSMo 59.563, which lets a recorder set an electronic format but does not require any recorder to offer one.

Deed Watch is a free alert service for property fraud. Visit DeedWatch.com, choose Newton County, Missouri, enter and confirm an email address, then add your search terms, such as your name or parcel. You are notified when recording activity matches.

Owners of a vacant, inherited or rented house benefit most, because nobody on site is likely to notice a forged deed or a lien filed against the property. The recorder also posts instructions for reporting suspicious recording activity.

Newton County lies in the southwest corner of Missouri inside the Joplin metro area, and Neosho is the seat. The population was 58,648 in the 2020 count, and the July 2025 estimate is 62,263, up 6.1 percent from April 2020. There are 25,333 housing units, and 76.6 percent of households own their home. A typical home is valued at $190,700, median gross rent is $817 and median household income is $66,301. Cities include Neosho, Seneca, Granby, Diamond and Fairview. Because three of every four households own, most deals here are owner-to-buyer transfers that end at this recorder's counter.

This counter cannot clear a title. It is the place to confirm that a deed of trust has a recorded release, that a plat or survey for the parcel is on file, and that a tax lien has been filed or released. Releases and assignments must cite the book and page of the paper they refer to.

For anything beyond that, such as who holds a valid claim, bring in an attorney or a title searcher. Sellers of an inherited or tenant-occupied house often begin with a title search to learn which recorded papers need a release before a buyer can close. A delinquent tax sale also runs each August, so a parcel with unpaid taxes can carry extra recorded history.

sections.h2: Courthouse offices and the tax bill
sections.html:
Several county offices share the courthouse, so one trip can cover them all. Ask each for current figures.

  • The assessor, Suite 205, (417) 451-8228, values real and personal property for tax purposes and is staffed on weekdays until 4:30.
  • The collector, Suite 203, (417) 451-8217, issues tax bills and runs the delinquent tax sale on the fourth Monday of August.
  • The county clerk, (417) 451-8221, can tell you where a valuation appeal is filed. The Board of Equalization is among the boards the commission appoints.

A tax obligation is fixed on January 1, the law gives no pro-rating, and the current owner is responsible for taxes due. Ask your closing office how the year's bill is split on the settlement sheet, and ask the collector what is still unpaid before you sign. Bills are mailed November 1 and turn delinquent after midnight on December 31. If you sell for cash, the payoff and the split are still handled at closing, just without a lender waiting on the paperwork.

faqs.q: Is a transfer tax collected on Newton County deeds?
faqs.a: None appears on the county fee page, which lists recording charges only. Ask your closing agent whether anything else is owed on your sale.

faqs.q: What is the cutoff for same-day recording at the Neosho courthouse?
faqs.a: Be at the counter by 3:30 pm. Staff stay until 4:30, but new recordings are taken only until 3:30, and later arrivals go on the record the next business day.

faqs.q: Can the recorder tell me who owns a house at a street address?
faqs.a: Records are searched by name, legal description or recording reference, and staff cannot give legal advice. For a parcel by address, the assessor at (417) 451-8228 is the better first call.

faqs.q: How can I send documents without driving to Neosho?
faqs.a: Mail them to P.O. Box 604 or use electronic recording through iCounty Technologies at (816) 295-1540. The office keeps up to $10 of any overpayment, so include enough to cover the fee.

faqs.q: What if my paper does not meet the layout rules?
faqs.a: The recorder may reject it and send it back with the reason, or record it with the $25 nonstandard charge added to the page fees.
